page: Microsoft Azure D32ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DADSv5 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a 1229 GB local SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng single-core tests and high image processing scores in Geekbench. Passmark memory benchmarks also place the memory subsystem in the top tier. However, multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the server shows strong text generation speeds with small LLM models, but struggles with larger models, yielding weak prompt processing performance on 70B parameter models.

From a resource density perspective, the D32ads_v5 offers a balanced hardware profile that avoids the premium costs associated with specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated instances. The inclusion of a generous 1229 GB local SSD provides high-speed local scratch space without requiring additional storage attachments. The primary tradeoff lies in its average multi-threaded scaling and limited capacity for heavy parallel computing or large-scale AI inference, which may require scaling up to compute-optimized or GPU-enabled tiers.

This instance is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including web serving, software compilation, medium-sized database operations, and moderate data processing tasks. The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC cores and local SSD storage also makes it an effective choice for application servers, development environments, and containerized microservices.
